mn22:3.27: Then we went up to Ariṭṭha and said to him,
mn22:3.28: ‘Is it really true, Reverend Ariṭṭha, that you have such a harmful misconception—
mn22:3.29: As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, the acts that he says are obstructions are not really obstructions for the one who performs them’?
mn22:3.30: When this was said, sir, Ariṭṭha said to us,
mn22:3.31: ‘Indeed, reverends. As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, the acts that he says are obstructions are not really obstructions for the one who performs them.’
mn22:3.32: Then, sir, wishing to dissuade Ariṭṭha from his view, we pursued, pressed, and grilled him,
mn22:3.33: ‘Don’t say that, Ariṭṭha! Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.
mn22:3.34: In many ways the Buddha has said that obstructive acts are obstructive, and that they really do obstruct the one who performs them.
mn22:3.35: The Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.
mn22:3.36: With the similes of a skeleton …
mn22:3.37: a cobra’s head, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.’
mn22:3.38: But even though we pursued, pressed, and grilled him in this way, sir, Ariṭṭha obstinately stuck to his misconception and insisted on it:
mn22:3.39: ‘Indeed, reverends. As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, the acts that he says are obstructions are not really obstructions for the one who performs them.’
